unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept the full ironic contrast: what any sane man would have done versus what Tommy did. The revision deletes the 'ought to have done' sentence and 'something seemed to snap in his brain'. Only 'What he did was entirely foreign...' remains, so the balanced mock-judicial turn is gone.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V6 and 'sober common sense' survive, so the essential beat is present.

evidence.quote: What he ought to have done, what any sane man would have done, was to remain patiently where he was and wait for his man to come out again.
What he ought to have done, what any sane man would have done, was to remain patiently where he was and wait for his man to come out again.
It was at this juncture that Tommy lost his head. What he did was entirely foreign to the sober common sense which was, as a rule, his leading characteristic.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'What he ought to have done...come out again.' sentence, and change 'What he did was' back to 'What he did do was'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (essential: 'against his usual sober common sense'; V6 purpose)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: V6 is meant to signal the impulsive break in Tommy's character. The narrator's measured, amused reproof is what makes the break comic and characterful. Without it, the passage reads as flat statement.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Narrator's 'ought to have done / did do' antithesis halved

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The opening sets up the bookish fantasy of leaping into another taxi. When it actually happens outside Lyons', the source and first draft give Tommy 'Follow that other taxi. Don't lose it.' The revision cuts the line, so the novel-reading premise is never visibly enacted.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The peremptory hand still implies the move. The plan allows cutting Whittington's directions to his driver, but not Tommy's line.

evidence.quote: “Follow that other taxi,” directed the young man. “Don’t lose it.”
"Follow that other taxi," directed the young man. "Don't lose it."
In books, you simply leapt into another, promised the driver a sovereign--or its modern equivalent--and there you were.
Outside, Whittington hailed a taxi, and another was drawing up to the curb in obedience to Tommy's peremptory hand.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert the eight-word line '"Follow that other taxi," directed the young man. "Don't lose it."' after revision paragraph 19.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: optional tradeoff misapplied: the plan's optional cut covers Whittington's directions, not this line
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The setup-payoff joke (book technique meets reality, then reality briefly obliges) disappears. The taxi worry becomes a dropped thread rather than a closed comic loop.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Taxi premise loses its comic payoff line
